recent.question: Chicago WS wins
recent.what_happened: The White Sox came back from 0-2 down to beat Cleveland 4-3 at Progressive Field in ALDS Game 2 and lead the series 2-0. Opener Anthony Kay was followed by Sean Burke, who allowed one hit in 4⅔ innings of bulk relief. Braden Montgomery's two-run double in the 6th gave Chicago the lead, and Grant Taylor closed out the 9th.
recent.what_we_missed: We didn't miss much. Our 0.50 was above the market's 0.405 and leaned the right way. The research did flag Venable's opener/bulk plan for Burke. What it didn't anticipate was that Grant Taylor would be available to close despite throwing 4 innings in Game 1.
recent.lesson: When a road team is close to evenly matched, has momentum, and has a believable plan for its pitching staff, a near-50% forecast above a market around 40% is reasonable. Don't push toward the home-favorite price just because of seeding.

suggested_change.change: No process change is needed. This is a well-calibrated forecast that came out on the side we leaned toward. Sources: https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/white-sox-vs-guardians-updates-170048164.html, https://www.foxsports.com/mlb/alds-game-2-chicago-white-sox-vs-cleveland-guardians-oct-05-2026-game-boxscore-97203

recent.question: Will André do Prado win the second-most votes in the 2026 São Paulo Senate election?
recent.what_happened: On October 4, Derrite (PP) finished first with 30.59% (13.27M votes) and André do Prado (PL) finished second with 29.28% (12.70M votes). Both Tarcísio-backed candidates won easily. Simone Tebet came third with 19.23% and Marina Silva fourth with 18.12%, so Prado's second place was not close.
recent.what_we_missed: The facts pointed toward Prado: Salles dropped out and endorsed the Derrite–Prado pair, the left's vote was split between two Lula-backed candidates, and in 2018 the late polls understated the right-wing Senate candidate in SP. Yet the forecaster went with the Quaest and Paraná Pesquisas polls that had Prado fourth and gave 0.45, below the market's 0.654, without a real reason to doubt the market.
recent.lesson: In two-seat Senate races where one side has a tight joint ticket and the other side's vote is split between two candidates, expect the joint-ticket pair to finish 1–2, and give that more weight than individual noisy polls with many undecided voters.

suggested_change.change: When polls are a multi-way technical tie, explicitly weigh coalition structure: ticket voting, vote splitting on one side, late dropouts consolidating votes, and the governor's coattails. Also require a stated reason before forecasting more than 15 points against the market.

recent.question: Will MrBeast's next video get 100 million or more views on day 2?
recent.what_happened: "Eat Everything In A Grocery Store, Win $1,000,000" set MrBeast's record for first-day views with about 72 million in 24 hours. Coverage soon after put it at about 90.8 million, and it went on to pass 100 million within 48 hours, so the market resolved YES.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecaster had no facts and guessed 36% from a general base rate. The video was already out and getting record first-day numbers, which the 0.895 market price reflected. A single search would have turned up reports of the record.
recent.lesson: If a view-count market is judged while its window is already running, check the current view count and pace first. Without that data, don't bet strongly against a market price near 90%.

suggested_change.change: Block or shrink bets that move more than 30 points away from the market price when the forecaster has no researched facts, especially on live-metric questions where the market may already see partial results.

recent.question: Will "Digger" Opening Weekend Box Office be between 9m and 11m?
recent.what_happened: Digger's actual Friday gross, previews included, came in around $3.3M rather than the $4M early projection. By Sunday the studio estimate for the weekend was about $8M, and rivals expected the final number nearer $7.5M, so it landed well below the $9–11M bracket.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecast relied on Deadline's early-Friday $4M number and its matching ~$10M weekend projection. By midday Saturday that had already been revised down. The market's 6% price showed traders had the lower Friday figure, and the forecaster's 67% ignored that signal.
recent.lesson: When a box-office market trades far below what your latest article implies, assume the Friday figure has been revised and check for the newest Saturday update before going against the market.

suggested_change.change: If the forecast differs from the market price by more than 40 points on a market that resolves within days, require a check for fresher data (for example a Saturday-morning box-office update), or else shrink the forecast toward the market price.

recent.question: Will "Digger" Opening Weekend Box Office be less than 9m?
recent.what_happened: Digger opened to about $8M from 3,321 theaters, well under $9M, so the market resolved YES. Its $4M Friday (including $1.2M in previews) led to only a ~2.0x weekend multiple, which fits a front-loaded opening for a poorly received film.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecaster leaned on the early '~$10M' weekend figure that Deadline and Forbes based on Friday's number. By midday Saturday the market was at 93.5% for under $9M, which suggests updated Saturday projections or trade chatter had already lowered the estimate. The forecaster also didn't check whether a 2.5x multiple from a $4M Friday that included previews made sense for a bomb with weak word of mouth and a much stronger competitor in Verity.
recent.lesson: When a weekend projection sits close to a bracket line and the market strongly disagrees, look for the newest Saturday or Sunday trade updates before trusting a Friday-based figure. Also apply low multiples, around 2.0–2.3x, to adult-skewing bombs whose Friday total includes previews.

suggested_change.change: For box-office brackets, require a search for the latest same-day trade updates (Deadline's Saturday or Sunday figures, Box Office Mojo, Variety), and when the forecast differs from the market by more than 40 points, require a check of the Friday-to-weekend multiple against comparable bombs.

recent.question: Rashee Rice: 1+ touchdowns
recent.what_happened: Rashee Rice played and caught a short pass on the Chiefs' second drive, then injured his hamstring in the first quarter and didn't return. Kansas City won 30-27 without him. Because he had taken snaps, the market settled on touchdowns scored and resolved No.
recent.what_we_missed: Nothing before the game pointed to the injury. He had practiced fully and had no injury designation. Still, the 0.53 forecast was well above the 0.385 market price on thin evidence: Rice had 1 touchdown in 3 games, and Kelce, with 2 receiving touchdowns, was also competing for red-zone targets. Going above 50% wasn't justified.
recent.lesson: For an 'anytime touchdown' prop on a receiver, start near the market price and only move far above it if there's clear evidence of heavy red-zone use, because a single game is close to a coin flip and outside events like injuries add downside risk.

suggested_change.change: When a forecast on an anytime-touchdown prop is more than 10 points above the market, require specific red-zone target or usage data to back it, or else shrink the forecast toward the market price.

recent_wins.question: Tyler Shough: 250+ passing yards
recent_wins.what_happened: On Monday Night Football the Falcons beat the Saints 45-24. Shough threw for 286 yards, including a late touchdown to Devaughn Vele, which cleared the 250 line by 36 yards.
recent_wins.what_worked: Research raised the forecast from 0.32 to 0.75 using current-season facts: about 44 attempts and 305 yards per game, 250+ in all three 2026 starts, Atlanta ranked 29th in passing yards allowed, and Etienne on IR, which made a pass-heavy plan more likely. The lopsided loss also helped, since trailing teams pass more and much of Shough's yardage likely came late, so part of the margin came from how the game went.
recent_wins.lesson: For QB yardage props, look at current-season attempt volume, the opponent's pass-defense rank and injuries in the QB's own backfield rather than older career game logs. A team that is likely to trail, or has lost its running backs, will tend to throw more, which supports the over.

suggested_change.change: Always pull the QB's current-season attempts per game, the opponent's pass-defense rank and the game spread, and give these more weight than last season's splits, because the no-research forecast (0.32) leaned on the 2025 log and missed.

recent_wins.question: Brian Robinson: 50+ rushing yards
recent_wins.what_happened: Atlanta beat New Orleans 45-24. Brian Robinson Jr., Bijan Robinson's backup, ran for 62 yards and 3 touchdowns, so the market resolved YES. Bijan ran for 145 yards on 19 carries.
recent_wins.what_worked: Very little of the research applied. Every player fact was about Bijan Robinson, a different player from the Brian Robinson named in the market. That error pushed the forecast up to 0.64. Only two facts were relevant to Brian: the Saints' run defense ranked 27th and Atlanta's run game ranked 2nd. That matchup left room for a backup to get carries, and a 45-24 blowout delivered them.
recent_wins.lesson: Before using any stats, check that the player in the research matches the player in the market's name exactly. Brian Robinson Jr. is not Bijan Robinson. Also treat a market price near 0.20 for a star's 50-yard line as a sign you may have the wrong player.

suggested_change.change: Add a gate that blocks a bet when the full name in the researched facts doesn't match the market's player name, or when the forecast differs from a liquid player-prop price by more than about 3x without a stated reason.

recent_wins.question: New York Y wins
recent_wins.what_happened: The Rays beat the Yankees 5-2 in ALDS Game 2 at Tropicana Field and took a 2-0 series lead. The Yankees made four errors, three of them on the first four batters Cam Schlittler faced, and three of Tampa Bay's five runs were unearned. Freddy Peralta allowed one run in 4 2/3 innings.
recent_wins.what_worked: The researched forecast leaned against the Yankees at 0.38 while the market had them at 0.535. Its reasons were real: the Rays had home field, Aaron Judge was off the roster, Peralta was in top form, and Tampa Bay's pitching had just held New York scoreless. But the Yankees didn't lose on any of those. They lost on fielding mistakes nobody could forecast, against the best road starter in MLB, so the result mostly reflects how random a single baseball game is.
recent_wins.lesson: For a single MLB game, treat a 15-point gap from the market as low-confidence unless the research turns up a concrete edge, such as a lineup or injury change the market hasn't priced. Don't count a win like this one as proof the method works.

suggested_change.change: Shrink single-game MLB forecasts toward the market price, which was close to 50/50 here, unless the research cites a specific fact the market hasn't absorbed, and cap bet size in those cases.

recent_wins.question: Digger Rotten Tomatoes score? (Above 50)
recent_wins.what_happened: Digger (2026, Iñárritu/Cruise) had a Tomatometer of 51% from 257 reviews over its opening weekend. The score stayed above 50 through the Monday 10:00 AM ET check, so the market resolved YES. My search only confirmed earlier readings of 52–53% from about 99 reviews. I didn't see the exact score at resolution time; the YES outcome implies it was 51% or higher.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research read the right page (/m/digger_2026, not the 1993 film at /m/digger) on the day before resolution and found 51% from 257 reviews. With a large review count, one more day of new reviews can't move the percentage much. The 79→257 review path (52→53→51%) showed the score was drifting only slightly. That supported 0.79 against a market price of 0.625. Still, a 51% score against a >50 line left very little room, so part of the win was luck.
recent_wins.lesson: Close to resolution, take the current score and review count from the correct resolution URL and estimate how many points one more day of reviews could shift it. Don't rely on the general sense that a film is 'rotten'.

suggested_change.change: For Rotten Tomatoes threshold markets, always record the exact review count and recent drift, and calculate how many negative reviews in a row would push the score below the strike before resolution.

recent_wins.question: Will Bitcoin reach $86,000 September 28-October 4?
recent_wins.what_happened: On Oct 2, 2026, a weak US jobs report (29,000 payrolls added against roughly 84,000 expected) sent Bitcoin above $87,000 to about $87,206 before it fell back toward $84–85k. That cleared the $86,000 threshold inside the Sept 28–Oct 4 window, two days before the forecast was made, so the market resolved YES.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research found several reports that BTC had already traded above $87k on Oct 2. That is more than $1,000 over the threshold, so Binance BTC/USDT almost certainly printed a 1-minute high at or above $86k. The question was effectively settled before judgment, and the 0.28 market price was stale or mispriced. Without the research, the forecaster gave only 0.31.
recent_wins.lesson: For 'will price reach X' questions judged late in the window, first check whether the high has already been hit during the window. If it overshot by a wide margin, a single-exchange rule doesn't change the answer, so forecast near-certain instead of settling at 0.7.

suggested_change.change: When research shows the threshold was already crossed by a clear margin after market creation and inside the window, push the forecast to about 0.95 or higher rather than discounting it for unnamed exchanges, because the major exchanges trade within a few dollars of each other.

recent_wins.question: Full Game: over 55.5 points scored? (Over 55.5 points)
recent_wins.what_happened: The Chiefs beat the Raiders 30-27 on Oct 4, 2026, for a 57-point total. That cleared the 55.5 line by only 1.5 points, so the market resolved YES.
recent_wins.what_worked: The researched forecast (0.57) took both teams' strong 3-0 offenses seriously (KC about 29 points a game, LV 88 points scored, including a 62-point game against the Saints) and correctly dismissed the fake '24-10' snippet. Still, 55.5 looks like an alternate line well above where the main total probably sat, likely in the high 40s. The 28.5% market price was the more reasonable estimate, and the game only got over by one late field goal's worth of points, so the 0.57 call was overconfident and paid off by luck.
recent_wins.lesson: For alternate totals well above the main line, start from the market's or the main line's implied distribution, and only move far from it if you have a specific reason such as weather, injuries to the defense, or pace. Early-season points per game from three games is not enough reason on its own.

suggested_change.change: Have research pull the consensus main game total and spread, so the forecaster can see how far the question's line sits from the main total before it departs from a low market price.

rules.rule: Read crypto rules for the exact strike, venue/pair (e.g. Binance BTC/USDT) and test (any touch or a close at a set candle), restate the strike up top, measure each price fact against it, and record a timestamped spot from that venue under an hour old for same-day windows.

For crypto threshold questions, report percent distance from spot to strike, hours left, realized volatility over a similar span, any weekend in the window, and timestamped same-day macro catalysts (yields, dollar, oil, jobs data), or state that none was found.

When judged mid-window, first check whether the strike was already reached inside the window: cite dated reports of the high and its margin past the strike, confirm on the resolution venue's candles where possible, and treat earlier-week moves as background.

For single-match win questions, confirm in the rules whether only a regulation-time win counts and state that a draw resolves No; check the actual venue, since a listed home side may play at a neutral ground, and report each side's results in this competition.

For match questions, report the current-season head-to-head with its game count (under about 10 games is small; note source disagreements) and each side's dated, sourced absences and returns; when injury sources disagree, check the confirmed matchday squad or lineup.
Discard any search snippet claiming a match result that is undated or dated before kickoff; report a result only from sources published after the match was played.

For tennis completion questions, read which endings count as not completed, report the tour level's historical share of matches finished normally, and count as risk only dated past-week injury, withdrawal or retirement news, labeling older or workload concerns weak.

Once a tennis match's start time has passed, check results sites (Tennis Explorer, ITF, tour site) for w/o or ret. markers first; before it, check the latest order of play and withdrawal lists, and report recent full matches each player finished.

For player touchdown props, use only facts on the named player; split rushing from receiving or passing TDs, report his share of team carries or targets inside the 5, his multi-season games-with-a-TD rate, and the team's run-pass split; label a few-game streak as small sample.

For single MMA fights, report each fighter's age, recent opponents and how those fights ended, and dated weigh-in or weight-cut news; label win streaks and common-opponent comparisons as weak evidence.

For single MLB games, report both confirmed starters' season ERA and ERA+ and recent starts, each team's season record, late-season form (record and offense since Sept 1) and home field; if it is a bullpen game, note that an opener's few innings carry little weight.

For playoff series and games, give the series score, what the trailing team still needs and where, earlier games' margins, current-season records and head-to-head, and whether standing rests on seeding; label past seasons' playoff records as small-sample background.

For in-round golf leader questions, pull the live hole-by-hole leaderboard and, for the named player and everyone within about 3 shots, report score, holes left and tee wave, plus the field's scoring average and how the rules settle a tie for the lead.

For golf tournament winner questions, report the player's world ranking, pro starts and wins, the field's strength and size, and his prior-week schedule (e.g. a team event); label team-event results and a single pro win as weak evidence of dominance.

For video view questions, record when the question opened, check the channel's upload list and news for any video posted since then, and report its upload time, hours elapsed in the window, current views and any reported view milestones or pace.

For view-count bracket questions, build reference figures only from first-168-hour counts of the channel's recent comparable uploads; label cumulative or lifetime totals, figures with unclear snapshot dates, and months-old uploads as not the resolution metric.

For Rotten Tomatoes score questions, read the year-specific film page named in the rules, record the score, review count and dated earlier readings showing drift, and count how many negative reviews would move it past the strike before the check time.

When a count question resolves on one named data provider, pull that provider's own trailing 2–4 week figures and write down its counting method (e.g. AIS-visible only) first; set aside other trackers' figures that count differently.

retro.headline: A quiet half-day: few new markets settled, nearly everything is still open, and I'm making no changes so the experiments already running can finish cleanly. Calibrated is the only strategy with a positive record, and no forecaster beats the market price.
went_well: Calibrated is up $1.4k (+$4.9 per $100 staked) on 10 settled bets since the 30c floor, winning 7 of them. It is also 7 for 7 on favourites (60c and up), +$5.0k. That is still under 30 bets, so it's an experiment, not a finding.
On 30-60c coin flips, main is +$5.0k on 12 settled bets and original +$0.8k on 10. That price band is where Jev + research has made money so far.

The long-shot floor still looks right. Every strategy's under-30c bets are deeply negative: main 0 wins in 9 (-$18.4k), bold 2 in 24 (-$19.2k), Jev alone bold 0 in 11 (-$21.7k). Nothing argues for lowering it.
went_badly: Nobody beats the market. On the 463 markets every forecaster answered, the market's Brier score is 0.148, against 0.188 for Claude direct, 0.214 for Jev + research and 0.254 for Jev alone (lower is better).

Tuning main hasn't paid per dollar yet. On the bets both placed, main loses $21.4 per $100 staked (-$8.7k on 16 settled) and original loses $19.7 per $100 (-$11.6k on 22 settled). Main has lost less in total only because it bet less.

Bold is still the worst strategy: -$26.9k all time on 59 settled bets, and -$4.7k on its first 5 settled (1 win) under the 0.35 info gate. Bold also loses on favourites: 5 of its 10 bets at 60c and up lost, for -$5.5k.

ideas_for_joey.title: Claimed edge vs realised return
ideas_for_joey.why: Every source is worse than the market, yet each bet claims at least 8c of edge. Bucketing settled 30c+ bets by claimed edge (8-12c, 12-20c, 20c+) and showing win rate and P&L per $100 would show whether big claimed edges are real edges or big errors. That would tell us whether to raise or lower min_edge.

ideas_for_joey.title: Calibrated vs main on the same markets
ideas_for_joey.why: Calibrated's profit (+$3.4k on 9 settled since the floor) contrasts with its Brier of 0.210, slightly worse than raw Jev + research at 0.2065. So its edge may come from which bets it picks and how it sizes them, or it may be luck. A paired comparison would show whether the calibration itself earns money before anyone considers moving main onto it.
